note: Independent source rejudgment. RFC 8955 Section 4.2.1.1 (rfc/full/rfc8955.txt:354-356): "In the first operator octet of a sequence, it MUST be encoded as unset and MUST be treated as always unset on decoding." Read both tagged units. internal/component/bgp/plugins/nlri/flowspec/types_test.go::TestRFC8955FirstOperatorAndBitTreatedUnsetOnDecode parses 05 05 01 50 81 16 and the otherwise identical 05 05 41 50 81 16, requires both accepted, pins the clear form to [[=80],[=22]], and requires identical decoded destination-port terms for the set form. The only input difference is the first AND bit; this observes semantic OR grouping, not merely acceptance. The changed quoted sentence now correctly says MUST, not the obsolete SHOULD wording. internal/component/bgp/plugins/nlri/flowspec/rfc8955_text_encode_reserved_test.go::TestRFC8955TextLeadingAndEncodedUnset directly constructs a first FlowMatch with And=true and requires exact wire 03 09 80 02; it also rejects text &syn and requires syn &ack to encode 05 09 00 02 c0 10, so the position rule is not confused with disabling AND everywhere. Producers read: internal/core/bgp/nlri/flowspec/types_numeric.go::writeToAFI clears first AND using i>0, and parseNumericComponent stores first And=false using len(matches)>0; internal/core/bgp/nlri/flowspec/format.go::FormatNumericMatches groups parsed terms; plugin_decode.go flowSpecToJSON/componentToJSON reaches that formatter; plugin_encode_text.go::parseBitmaskTermsText rejects a leading join. Encoding and decoding clauses are both asserted. The decode observation does not independently discriminate removal of the parser guard because the formatter also interprets a leading term independently; that redundant guard break is not claimed as proof of semantic noncompliance. The existing native record for the encoding test halts writeToAFI and proves reach, not a specific AND-bit mutation. No fresh checks or native discrimination run by this auditor; parent owns that proof.
